fields.question: Topic 1, what milestone 4 is for. Which goal should milestone 4 have? I recommend Orchestration. It is the next layer in the founding plan, and it replaces the orchestrator session that still does this by hand. Milestone 3's gaps would be its first change sets, because Rhiza can't orchestrate runs that still break.

fields.question: Topic 3a, milestone 4's done points, following milestone 3's pattern. Proposed: (1) Milestone 5's first change sets are shipped with `rhiza daemon` orchestrating and no orchestrator session: you accept plans, answer the inbox and sign off, nothing else. (2) Runs hold up: a build, review or ship-change run finishes without hand repair (no hand-made render commit, no second run on one change set, no swept-up actor records). (3) make check stays green, rhiza check included, reads within budget, and the default test run binds no socket. Do these three done points fit?

fields.question: Topic 3b, which existing drafts serve milestone 4? There are 15 draft gap change sets: milestone 3's 8 (agents never start runs, split Leaf trailers, build/review render, failed fixer's cycle, message a busy session, plan capture on done, questions not permissions, token printout) plus 7 older ones (builder actor records, findings numbering lock, one live run per change set, the guide-install flake, review status in Rex, idle check actors, workflow-step limits as constraints). I recommend all 15, because the daemon can only ship work unattended if these runs hold up. I also recommend the proposed backlog item 'watches runs and passes their questions to the owner with a recommendation' as the inbox's change set.

fields.question: Topic 4a, the new change sets. Besides the 15 gap drafts and the inbox change set (the existing proposed one, 01M5SWTKV6), I propose two new ones: (A) The daemon: `rhiza daemon` starts ship-change runs on accepted, ready change sets in milestone order under a cap, each run in its own Rex tab, picks up after a restart from the run journals, and shows `rhiza daemon status`. It depends on the draft 'one live run per change set'. (B) Usage-limit pause: a run whose agent session hits the Claude usage limit waits for the reset and then continues the session, instead of failing. Are these the right new change sets?

fields.question: Topic 5a, when does a run stop counting as live for 'one live run per change set'? I recommend: until its journal says it finished (done or failed). An interrupted run whose process died still counts, so `rhiza run start` refuses, names that run and points you to `rhiza run resume`. That way nobody starts a second run over a half-done one.

fields.question: Topic 5b, with interrupted runs counting as live, a run you want to give up on would block its change set for good. I recommend adding `rhiza run abandon <run>`, which journals the run as failed with an 'abandoned by <actor>' detail, so a new run can start. It refuses a run that has finished, and leaves the worktree and branch alone.

fields.question: Topic 6b, how does the daemon run and launch work? I recommend: `rhiza daemon` runs in the foreground of whatever Rex tab you start it in, one per repo (a lock under the git common dir), polling the roadmap and run journals every few seconds with no socket. It starts each run as `rhiza run start <cs>` in a new Rex tab, so a run outlives a daemon restart. `--max-runs` defaults to 2, `--autonomous` passes through to every run it starts, and `rhiza daemon status` reads a state file.

fields.question: Topic 7a, where are inbox questions answered? I recommend: `rhiza inbox` lists every item (question, sign-off, failed run) across runs, oldest first, and `rhiza inbox open <item>` focuses the asking session's Rex tab, so you answer in the agent's own menu with its context in view. Sign-offs are approved or sent back from the inbox through the existing approve and request-changes commands.

The inbox shows it beside the question, and the run never waits for it.
